title: Prompt, retrieve or fine-tune: how practitioners actually decide
summary: The three ways to change what a model does — prompting, retrieval and fine-tuning — and how practitioners choose between them: evals and a break-even number first, then sorting failures into knowledge problems and behavior problems. Why fine-tuning is an unreliable way to add facts (Ovadia, Gekhman, LIMA), where it earns its keep (format, consistency, cost, RAFT-style reading skill), and what OpenAI's self-serve fine-tuning wind-down and Anthropic's homeopathic-learning result add to the decision.

topics: deep dive: prompt, retrieve or fine-tune — how practitioners decide
concepts_taught: choosing between prompting, retrieval and fine-tuning: evals and a business break-even first (OpenAI's 81.5% customer-service example), then sorting failures into knowledge problems (context optimization, maximizes accuracy) and behavior problems (LLM optimization, maximizes consistency), with model swapping as the zeroth lever

why fine-tuning is an unreliable way to inject facts: RAG beat unsupervised fine-tuning on new current-events facts (Ovadia: Mistral 7B 48% base, 87.5% RAG, 50% fine-tuned, 59% with ten paraphrases), new-knowledge examples are learned slower and linearly raise hallucination (Gekhman), and LIMA's claim that knowledge comes from pre-training

when retrieval is needed at all and how it fails separately: whole-corpus-in-context under ~200K tokens with prompt caching, long context beating RAG on average at higher cost (Self-Route), measuring retriever recall separately, and retrieval hurting a behavior problem (OpenAI Icelandic: fine-tuned GPT-4 87 BLEU, 83 with RAG)

where fine-tuning earns its keep: format and instruction consistency, smaller cheaper models with shorter prompts, RAFT's training on golden-plus-distractor documents to read the open book, LoRA practice (all layers, ~10x learning rate), and fine-tuning-specific risks: homeopathic learning in data mixtures and hosted-platform availability (OpenAI's self-serve wind-down)

lore.note: Alan holds that fine-tuning isn't shrinking but moving — out of hosted APIs and into open-weight adapters you own — against Ada's reading that a large provider closing self-serve fine-tuning continues a curve from default to last resort. Left unresolved.
